_comment: Defaults for `dotnet lambda deploy-function`, so the deploy is one command rather than a line
of flags somebody has to remember correctly.
The runtime is provided.al2023, not dotnetNN. AWS's managed .NET runtimes follow the LTS
releases and lag them; this project targets net10.0, so rather than wait for a managed runtime
to appear the app ships its own copy of .NET inside the bundle. That is what --self-contained
does, and it is the supported way to run a .NET version Lambda does not manage.
It also means the runtime never changes underneath the shop. A managed runtime is patched by
AWS on their schedule; this one moves when you rebuild.
For a custom runtime the handler is the assembly name, not Type::Method.
// architecture: Graviton — cheaper per millisecond, and the build container here is arm64 already
// memory: CPU is handed out in proportion to memory, and sign-in runs PBKDF2 600k times. Below 1024 the first sign-in of the day is a visible pause.
// timeout: Catalogue import validates and writes thousands of rows in one request.
// function-url-auth-type: NONE is right: every route except sign-in and health is refused by the app's own session check, exactly as it is locally.
// environment-variables: Set these in the console or with --environment-variables; they are not kept here because the connection string is a credential.
